notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS (B2B) evaluating Redwood for their conversational/agent layer. Primary driver: migration from incumbent LLM API due to recent latency regressions affecting conversational UX (users noticing lag on streaming responses). They run high-concurrency chat agents integrated with tool-calling (search, DB lookups, ticket creation).

Benchmarking notes (internal harness v2):
- Redwood streaming: end-to-end median (p50) message-to-first-token ~170ms, p95 ~450ms (across 20K sessions, avg tokens per turn 45).
- Incumbent (current provider): p50 ~430ms, p95 ~980ms on same harness and infra.
- Tool-calling (function call to external service): Redwood added ~30-40ms overhead vs incumbent ~120-160ms (measured for JSON-serialized tool responses).
- Observations: Redwood's continuous streaming + KV cache reduced tail latency for multi-turn flows; incumbent showed spikes under bursty traffic.

Customer quotes and priorities:
- CTO: "Streaming latency needs to feel instantaneous for trial conversion. p95 matters more than p50."
- Head of Product: cares about tool-calling reliability and deterministic fallbacks when models degrade.

POC scope asked: 2-week hosted streaming POC (real traffic replay), followed by cost/throughput estimate for Dedicated pool. Will run A/B on small percentage of traffic if metrics look good. Key success metrics: p95 < 600ms for first-token, error rate <0.5%, cost neutral or lower than incumbent when accounting for caching.

Integration notes: SDK used (JS streaming + python backend), minor tokenizer differences required prompt adjustments, SE recommended prefix caching and per-route batching. Pricing conversation: procurement wants committed pricing floor and a clear burst policy.
